cim_eredeti: What Is DeepAI? Free AI Image Generator Explained, Plus 2026 Alternatives
szoveg_eredeti:
DeepAI has been online since late 2016, which makes it one of the oldest consumer AI image tools still running — it predates Midjourney, DALL·E 2, and Stable Diffusion by years. That history is exactly why it shows up in searches today: people land on deepai.org, see a plain interface that looks unchanged from an earlier era of AI, and want to know whether it is still worth using, what the free plan actually gives you, and what has replaced it since. This guide answers all three, with every number checked against DeepAI’s own pricing and tool pages this week, plus three current alternatives — Leonardo.Ai, Ideogram, and Krea — so you can decide where to generate your next image.

Figures are from DeepAI’s pricing page, Leonardo’s Tokens FAQ, Ideogram’s plans page, and Krea’s pricing page, all checked October 2026.

Krea's free plan runs Krea 2 image generation at 100 compute units a day, no credit card.

Every figure in this post comes from a page we loaded on October 5, 2026: DeepAI’s pricing page, its Text to Image tool page, and its about page, Leonardo’s Tokens FAQ, Ideogram’s plans and billing docs, and Krea’s own pricing page. For the popularity question specifically — “how many people use DeepAI” — we checked three independent traffic estimators (Similarweb, Semrush, and Ahrefs) rather than inventing a single number, because none of these tools publish an audited user count and the estimators disagree with each other by a wide margin, which we report plainly below instead of averaging it away. Every image in this post is a single, raw Krea 2 generation from the exact prompt printed beside it — made to illustrate the ideas in this piece, never to imitate a DeepAI, Leonardo, or Ideogram screenshot.

A raw Krea 2 generation illustrating “old tool, new tools” — not a real screenshot of any product.

DeepAI describes itself as “the all-in-one creative AI platform built for everyone.” Per its own about page, it “got our start in late 2016 with the first browser-based text-to-image generator,” which predates the current wave of consumer AI image tools by several years. Since then it has added an AI chat assistant with live web browsing, a photo editor, video generation, music generation, and a voice chat mode, all accessible from the same account.

The core product people search for is still the Text to Image generator: type a description, pick a style, and get an image back. DeepAI’s own tool page states “No Sign-Up Needed: Use all core features immediately — just enter a prompt and go,” which is the main reason the tool still gets traffic — most competitors gate even a first generation behind an account. The page also states that users retain “100% of the rights to everything you create, even on the free plan,” and that outputs carry no copyright restriction on commercial use.

Beyond the consumer product, DeepAI’s about page says it also takes on “custom technical projects for governments, nonprofits, and research organizations,” building computer vision systems for things like conservation and environmental monitoring under what it calls an “AI for Good” initiative. That side of the business is unrelated to the image generator most people land on the site for, but it explains why deepai.org also hosts a large library of machine-learning research paper summaries — a leftover from its original identity as a research-aggregation site before the image generator became its main draw.

Yes, with a real, no-account path: you can generate images on deepai.org without creating an account at all. That is a genuine point of difference from Leonardo.Ai, Ideogram, and Krea, which all require a free sign-up before your first generation.

What the free tier does not give you is DeepAI’s higher-quality resolution tiers. The Text to Image page lists four output tiers: Standard (the free default), HD at 640×640, Genius at 1024×1024, and Super Genius at full 2K — and the three higher tiers are gated behind DeepAI Pro. DeepAI’s own pricing page is explicit about the free plan’s shape: “Limited HD images and editing” and “Limited standard chat messages,” alongside a daily AI Voice Chat allowance of 60 seconds and limited video and music generation. DeepAI does not publish an exact daily generation cap on its pricing page, and third-party reviews disagree on the details — several report a handful of no-account generations before the site prompts for sign-up, which is worth confirming yourself if an exact number matters for your use case.

One detail that’s worth flagging honestly: whether free-tier images carry a watermark is not clearly stated on DeepAI’s own pricing or tool pages, and third-party reviews conflict on this point — some report no watermark on Standard images, others describe a watermark that Pro removes. We could not confirm a definitive policy from DeepAI’s own pages, so test a generation yourself before assuming either way.

DeepAI Pro, per the pricing page, costs $9.99/month billed monthly or $7.50/month billed annually, and includes:

Beyond the monthly allowance, DeepAI charges overage rates: $1 per 100 additional HD images, $1 per 350 additional chat messages, and 20¢ per additional second of HD video. The pricing page also states “Your price never changes — renews at the same rate, never higher,” which locks in your rate at signup even if list prices rise later.

Prompt (DeepAI Text to Image, free tier):

A cozy reading nook with a window seat, stacks of books, warm afternoon light, soft watercolor illustration style

Variation tips: DeepAI’s style selector matters more than wording tweaks on the free tier — try the same prompt across two or three of its built-in styles before rewriting it, since the underlying model responds more to style choice than to extra adjectives.

Reputation is mixed, and the split is fairly clean: people doing casual, quick, or hobbyist generations tend to report satisfaction; people comparing it against 2026’s frontier models for professional work do not. On Trustpilot, DeepAI holds a 3.8-out-of-5 rating across its review page as of this week, with reviewers commonly citing the low price of Pro and the straightforward interface as positives, and billing clarity and output quality as the most frequent complaints.

On image quality specifically, review sites that test DeepAI side-by-side with current-generation models consistently find it behind: models lag in fine detail, scene coherence, and anatomical accuracy compared with 2026’s leading image generators, and prompt adherence is moderate — complex prompts with multiple subjects more often produce merged or dropped elements than a clean composition. That tracks with DeepAI’s own position: it has not announced a new flagship image model in the way Leonardo, Ideogram, or Krea regularly do, so the gap between it and current frontier tools has widened since 2016 even though the product itself still works.

The honest read: DeepAI is a functional, no-friction tool for a quick, disposable image — a meme, a placeholder, a one-off illustration you won’t reuse. For anything that needs to hold up next to current AI-generated work — marketing creative, a portfolio piece, a client deliverable — the quality gap is the thing to weigh against its price and lack of sign-up friction.

A raw Krea 2 generation illustrating “an early AI tool still running in 2026” — not an actual photo of DeepAI’s product.

DeepAI does not publish an audited user count anywhere on its site, so any single figure claiming to answer this exactly is an estimate dressed up as a fact — and the estimates disagree with each other enough to prove the point. Checked this week: Similarweb’s own analytics page shows roughly 8.6 million visits to deepai.org over a trailing three-month window; Semrush’s site-traffic report shows 15.35 million visits in July 2026; and Ahrefs shows 35.9 million visits in August 2026. cim: Fiók nélkül is használható a veterán DeepAI képgenerátor
lead: A 2016 óta működő DeepAI regisztráció nélkül kínál ingyenes képgenerálást, de a képminőség elmarad a modern versenytársak mögött.
osszefoglalo:
A 2016-ban indult [DeepAI](https://deepai.org) az egyik legrégebbi fogyasztói AI-eszköz, amelynek legnagyobb előnye, hogy **fiók létrehozása nélkül** is lehetővé teszi a képgenerálást. Az ingyenes verzióban a felhasználók teljes kereskedelmi jogot kapnak az elkészült képekre, így azok szabadon felhasználhatók.

A szolgáltatás ingyenes változata ugyanakkor csak alacsony felbontású képeket készít, a jobb minőségű generálásokért pedig előfizetést kér. A havi 9,99 dolláros Pro csomag nagyobb felbontást és több funkciót ad, de a tesztek szerint a DeepAI képminősége így is **elmarad a modern modellek mögött**, mivel a fejlesztők régóta nem frissítették a mögötte álló motort.

Ha professzionális marketinganyagokhoz keresünk alternatívát, a [Krea](https://www.krea.ai) ingyenes csomagja napi **100 számítási egységet** biztosít a Krea 2 modell használatához. Emellett a [Leonardo.Ai](https://leonardo.ai/) és az [Ideogram](https://ideogram.ai) is jobb minőségű képeket kínál, bár ezeknél már kötelező a regisztráció.
miert_szamit: A DeepAI kiválóan alkalmas **gyors vázlatok és mémek azonnali elkészítésére** regisztrációs hercehurca nélkül. Komolyabb marketingkampányokhoz vagy ügyfélmunkákhoz azonban a gyengébb anatómiai pontosság miatt érdemesebb a **Krea vagy az Ideogram** eszközeit választani.
